anatomy.flutter: Drawer(trigger, content) is a StatefulWidget builder-callback API around OverlayPortal; DrawerContent/DrawerHandle/DrawerHeader/DrawerFooter/DrawerTitle/DrawerDescription are the panel parts, with NO DrawerBody widget — children stack directly in DrawerContent's Column.
anatomy.web: Drawer/DrawerTrigger/DrawerPortal/DrawerClose/DrawerOverlay/DrawerContent/DrawerHeader/DrawerBody/DrawerFooter/DrawerTitle/DrawerDescription are eleven exported compound-component pieces wrapping vaul's DrawerPrimitive.*, and DrawerBody supplies the only `min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto` scroll zone.
anatomy.note: Web has a DrawerBody scroll container that Flutter deliberately omits: the Dart file's own doc comment states the panel 'is the one panel in the family that is deliberately NOT scrollable' because a Scrollable would win the drag-gesture arena against drag-to-dismiss, and vaul's own scroll-position answer 'is not ported' — an intentional, documented simplification, not a missed port.

api.flutter: DrawerContent/DrawerHandle only style the bottom direction (`inset-x-0 bottom-0`, `mt-24`, `max-h-[80vh]`, `rounded-t-xl`); the file doc comment lists 'Not ported: the other three directions (vaul-drawer-direction left/right/top)... snapPoints; and the background-scale effect'.
api.web: DrawerContent's class list fully styles all four `data-[vaul-drawer-direction=bottom|left|right|top]` variants (widths, insets, radii, borders, sm:max-w-sm caps), and Drawer forwards `direction`, `dismissible`, `snapPoints` and vaul's other drag-tuning props straight through.
api.note: Flutter only implements the bottom direction the corpus actually uses, per its own doc comment ('no caller in the corpus asks for' the other directions); left/right/top, snapPoints and background-scale are explicitly flagged as not ported rather than silently dropped, so this is a tracked, intentional scope reduction.

states.flutter: _DrawerState tracks `_drag` and closes past `_height * _closeThreshold` where `_closeThreshold = 0.25` — the file's own comment calls this 'vaul's closeThreshold default — a quarter of the drawer's own height'.
states.web: The docs page's StateGrid enumerates rest/closed, hover, focus-visible, disabled trigger and open, noting loading/success/empty are N/A because 'the drawer is a container' whose outcome states belong to whatever action lives in DrawerBody.
states.note: Both sides model the same rest/open state pair plus a drag-release threshold pulled directly from vaul's own 0.25 default; loading/success/empty are correctly absent from both since neither treats the drawer itself as carrying those states.

disabled.flutter: Drawer takes only `trigger` and `content` builders and has no `enabled`/`disabled` field of its own; a disabled trigger is whatever Widget the caller passes (e.g. a Button with `onPressed: null`).
disabled.web: Drawer forwards to vaul's DrawerPrimitive.Root, which likewise has no disabled concept; the docs page's 'disabled trigger' state cell is just `<Button variant="secondary" disabled>` passed to DrawerTrigger.
disabled.note: Neither Drawer component owns a disabled state — it is entirely delegated to the trigger control on both platforms, so the dimension does not apply to the drawer itself.

interaction.flutter: RawGestureDetector's VerticalDragGestureRecognizer drives `_update`/`_end`; `_drag = (_drag + details.delta.dy).clamp(0.0, double.infinity)` makes the drag downward-only ('vaul dampens an upward drag... to nothing'), and Escape/focus-trap/scrim-tap dismissal come from the shared OverlayPortal (dialog.dart's `LogicalKeyboardKey.escape` handling and `Semantics(scopesRoute: true)`) that Drawer imports and composes.
interaction.web: vaul's own pointer/touch drag drives dismissal directly on DrawerPrimitive.Content; the docs page states 'Escape, a click on the overlay, and a drag past the dismiss threshold all close the drawer, plus any explicit DrawerClose control', matching Radix Dialog's own keyboard/overlay contract.
interaction.note: Both close on Escape, overlay tap, and a drag past threshold, and both trap focus inside the panel while open; Flutter inherits the Escape/focus-trap machinery from the same dialog.dart OverlayPortal every other modal in the family shares, rather than reimplementing it in drawer.dart.

semantics.flutter: DrawerTitle uses `TextStyles.h4` and DrawerDescription uses `TextStyles.body`, both centred (`TextAlign.center`); Drawer composes the same OverlayPortal/`Semantics(scopesRoute: true)` + `BlockSemantics()` infra as dialog.dart, so the panel is announced as a modal route the same way every other overlay in the family is.
semantics.web: The docs page states role="dialog" with aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby/aria-describedby pointed at DrawerTitle/DrawerDescription automatically, focus moving into the content and trapped there on open, returning to the trigger on close.
semantics.note: Both sides route accessible naming/description through a Title/Description pair and both trap focus and mark the panel as a modal region; the exact ARIA role vs Flutter's route-scoping Semantics node are platform-native equivalents of the same contract.
